design_summary.purpose: Top-level integration of firmware control, physics-based surrogate transport, safety validation, bounded actuator command generation, and bulk history storage for an active-aerodynamics controller operating over 20–55 m/s.
design_summary.operating_model: The design is organized around a firmware-visible MMIO control plane, a control core that validates vehicle speed and sensor health while managing model-request/model-response transport, and a technology-neutral history memory wrapper for bulk event storage. The top emits model-request valid/data, accepts model-request ready, accepts model-response valid/data, and emits model-response ready. When invalid, stale, timeout, reset, or fault conditions occur, actuator command validity is inhibited and the fault is latched for software handling; no fallback command behavior is introduced.

module_architecture.name: aero_mmio_csr_block
module_architecture.role: Firmware-visible CSR/MMIO decoder and register file implementing the control plane.
responsibilities: Decode every firmware-visible register through the MMIO interface.
Expose writable configuration for enable, speed bounds, actuator bounds, timeouts, and model selection.
Provide readable status for latched fault, safety inhibit, timeout activity, and last-command observability.
Generate the dedicated fault-clear pulse from the registered MMIO field.
Return coherent read data and ready/response semantics for firmware transactions.
interface_notes: Consumes mmio_valid, mmio_write, mmio_addr, and mmio_wdata from firmware.

Drives semantic configuration outputs cfg_enable, cfg_min_speed_mps, cfg_max_speed_mps, cfg_cmd_min, cfg_cmd_max, cfg_timeout_cycles, cfg_stale_limit_cycles, cfg_model_select, and cfg_fault_clear to the controller core.
Receives status inputs from the controller core and does not drive those status inputs.
ownership_notes: Owns the control-plane decode and readable/writable register contract.
No inaccessible internal state is presented as software-visible.
Does not implement actuator logic or model transport.

module_architecture.name: adaptive_aero_controller_core
module_architecture.role: Main control engine for validation, surrogate transport sequencing, command bounding, safety inhibition, and fault latching.
responsibilities: Validate operating-speed band and sensor freshness/health.
Emit model requests only when the controller has a valid control decision to request surrogate evaluation.
Accept model responses only through the declared ingress path while driving model_rsp_ready outward.
Bound actuator command values to configured min/max limits before asserting validity.
Latch faults and assert safety_inhibit on invalid, stale, timeout, reset, or sensor-fault conditions.
Capture history entries for recent requests, responses, and command decisions through the storage wrapper interface.
Expose last-command and timeout status for firmware observation.
interface_notes: Consumes configuration inputs from the CSR block.
Consumes vehicle_speed_mps, sensor_valid, sensor_fault, and sensor_stale from the external plant/sensor path.
Drives model_req_valid and model_req_data outward, accepts model_req_ready as backpressure, accepts model_rsp_valid/model_rsp_data as inputs, and drives model_rsp_ready outward.

Drives actuator_cmd_valid, actuator_cmd_data, fault_latched, safety_inhibit, status_last_cmd_valid, status_last_cmd_data, status_last_speed_mps, status_timeout_active, history_wr_en, history_wr_addr, and history_wr_data.
Consumes history_rd_data from the memory wrapper.
ownership_notes: Owns the bounded control decision and safety-state behavior.
Maintains the latched-fault state for software handling.
Does not create fallback or substitute commands.

module_architecture.name: adaptive_aero_history_wrapper
module_architecture.role: Technology-neutral bulk memory wrapper around the required SRAM macro for time-series payload and event history storage.
responsibilities: Instantiate the declared SRAM macro cell using the specified instance name.
Preserve storage as bulk memory rather than flattening it into registers.
Pass read data back to the controller core.
Support synchronous access under top-level clock and reset.
Remain compatible with FPGA block RAM inference or native macro mapping while preserving the explicit macro contract.
interface_notes: Consumes history_csb, history_we, history_addr, and history_din from the controller-side storage path.
Drives history_dout back to the controller core.
ownership_notes: Owns only the bulk-memory wrapper role.
Does not expose storage contents as firmware-visible registers.
Does not provide substitute memory behavior if macro binding is unavailable in a downstream flow.

interface_summary.intent: Provide the firmware-visible CSR/MMIO control plane with read/write and ready/response semantics.
Deliver decoded configuration and fault-clear control from firmware to the control core.
Return live status for firmware readback and observability.
Implement the mandated transport direction contract: request valid/data are outputs, request ready is an input, response valid/data are inputs, and response ready is an output.
Provide operating condition and sensor-health data used for validation and safe control decisions.
Emit bounded actuator commands only when all safety and freshness checks pass.
Write operational history and event payloads into the bulk-memory wrapper.
Return stored history data for controller-side use without flattening the storage into registers.

data_flow_summary: Firmware writes control registers through the MMIO CSR block and reads back status through the same interface.
The controller core consumes decoded configuration and external sensor inputs to decide whether a surrogate request should be issued.
Model-request traffic flows outward as model_req_valid/model_req_data, with model_req_ready arriving from the external model side.
Model-response traffic flows inward as model_rsp_valid/model_rsp_data, while model_rsp_ready is driven outward by the controller core.

If vehicle speed is outside the configured band, if sensor_valid is low, if sensor_fault or sensor_stale is asserted, or if timeout/stale limits are exceeded, the controller inhibits actuator_cmd_valid and latches the fault.
When control is allowed and a valid model response is accepted, the controller clamps the command to cfg_cmd_min/cfg_cmd_max before asserting actuator validity.
Operational events and time-series payloads are written into the history wrapper, which remains a bulk-memory structure rather than a register array.

clock_reset_summary.clocking: All modules are synchronous to clk.
clock_reset_summary.reset_behavior: reset_n is active-low and distributed to the MMIO block, controller core, and history wrapper. On reset, MMIO response/ready state returns to idle, model request and actuator validity are deasserted, the controller holds model response ready in the safe accept state required by sequencing, history strobes are inactive, configuration returns to safe defaults, and any fault or safety inhibit state is placed in a safe inhibited condition without generating any substitute actuator command.

integration_notes: The synthesizable top module remains adaptive_aero_control_top and must not be replaced by a status, telemetry, register-bank, or leaf module.
The MMIO control plane coexists with the streaming model transport and cannot be substituted by it.
Every declared firmware-visible register is reachable through decode; inaccessible internal state is not exposed as software-visible.
Bulk payload/history storage is kept in the technology-neutral memory wrapper so FPGA flows can map it to native block RAM.

No fallback command, fallback register, fallback status, fallback controller, substitute command, or fallback-on-reset behavior is introduced; invalid, stale, timeout, reset, or fault conditions inhibit actuator output validity and latch the fault for software handling.
The top-level output ports are described as being driven by real RTL sources; required outputs are not tied only to child inputs.
consistency_notes: No hierarchy, ports, or filenames may differ from digital_spec_json.
